title: 2025年6月 第1套

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Everything changed for 7-year-old Tariq when he slapped some butter on an ear of corn.
lines.translation: 当7岁的Tariq在一根玉米上抹了些黄油时，一切都改变了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He knew it tasted good, but butter made it better.
lines.translation: 他知道玉米本来就好吃,但黄油让它变得更美味。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: His passion for produce got him a position as South Dakota's official Corn Ambassador.
lines.translation: 他对农产品的热情为他赢得了南达科他州官方玉米大使的职位。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Tariq's profession of love for his favorite vegetable earned him the name "the Corn Kid".
lines.translation: 塔里克热爱他最爱的蔬菜 给他取名为"玉米小子"

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This was after his online interview attracted millions of views and was made into a song.
lines.translation: 这是在他在线采访吸引数百万人观看之后,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America.
lines.translation: 南达科他州是美国最大的玉米生产国之一。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The corn provides nourishment across the globe.
lines.translation: 玉米在全球各地提供营养。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Tariq said, "Not everyone has to like corn, but everyone should definitely try it, especially with butter." Tariq and his family were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony at the state's Corn Palace.
lines.translation: 塔里克和他的家人被邀请到南达科他州康纳宫参加荣誉仪式。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Officials wanted to highlight South Dakota's two largest industries: tourism and agriculture.
lines.translation: 官员们想强调南达科他州的两大产业:旅游业和农业。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Tariq couldn't believe his eyes when he saw the palace made of corn.
lines.translation: 塔里克看到宫殿里是玉米做的 眼睛就不敢相信了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题1和2是根据你刚刚听到的新闻报导提出的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 1. How did Tariq make corn taste better?
lines.translation: 第 1 题：Tariq 是如何让玉米味道更好的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 2. Why were Tariq and his family invited to South Dakota?
lines.translation: 第 2 题：为什么 Tariq 和他的家人被邀请到 South Dakota?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: News reports 2.
lines.translation: 2. 新闻报告2。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Two arrests were announced Thursday.
lines.translation: 星期四宣布了两起逮捕。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The arrests were in connection with a string of mail thefts from U.S.
lines.translation: 逮捕与一系列从美国偷来的邮件有关。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Postal Service's collection boxes in Marion County and for the possession of a stolen postal key, according to the Department of Justice.
lines.translation: 据司法部称,邮政局在马里昂县的收集箱和被盗邮政钥匙的藏箱。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman, both 23, were arrested after evidence gathered in an investigation showed the pair stole mail on multiple occasions using a postal key, according to a news release.
lines.translation: 据新闻稿称,23岁的Jordan Jax和Tarod Goodman在调查中收集的证据显示两人多次使用邮政钥匙盗窃邮件后被逮捕。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Jax and Goodman stole mail for around four months.
lines.translation: Jax和Goodman盗窃邮件约四个月。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Investigators reviewed videos of the collection boxes; the video showed the two men loading the stolen mail into Jax's vehicle.
lines.translation: 调查人员查看了收集箱的监控视频;视频显示两名男子将被盗邮件装入Jax的车辆。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Investigators were also able to recover the key that was used to open the collection boxes.
lines.translation: 调查人员还找回了用于打开收集箱的钥匙。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Jax and Goodman each face up to five years in federal prison in the mail thefts and up to ten years for possession of the postal key.
lines.translation: Jax和Goodman各自面临邮件盗窃罪最高五年联邦监禁,以及持有邮政钥匙罪最高十年监禁。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 3. What did Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman do according to a news release?
lines.translation: 第 3 题：根据一则新闻稿，Jordan Jax 和 Tarod Goodman 做了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 4. What do Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman face?
lines.translation: 第 4 题：Jordan Jax 和 Tarod Goodman 面临什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: News Report 3.
lines.translation: 《新闻报告3》。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Can fast-fashion be sustainable?
lines.translation: 快时尚能否实现可持续发展？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers think yes.
lines.translation: 研究人员认为可以。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Identifying why the fast-fashion business model creates waste and determining whether regulators can establish incentives for consumers and manufacturers are steps to reduce waste.
lines.translation: 确定快时尚商业模式为何会造成浪费，以及判断监管机构能否建立激励机制来引导消费者和制造商，是减少浪费的关键步骤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Recently, the clothing industry has come under attack for creating a waste problem with serious environmental consequences.
lines.translation: 近年来，服装行业因制造严重的环境后果的废物问题而受到抨击。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In the absence of environmentally and economically feasible recycling options, fast-fashion manufacturers pump out low-quality clothes produced in high volumes that are worn only a few times and then discarded.
lines.translation: 在缺乏环境和经济上可行的回收选择的情况下，快时尚制造商大量生产低质量的服装，这些服装只穿几次就被丢弃。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The researchers put forth policy contributions, ranging from sustainable disposal of leftover stock to production tax to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious.
lines.translation: 研究人员提出了一系列政策建议，从可持续处置剩余库存到征收生产税，以激励制造商和消费者更加注重减少浪费。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In order to devise effective policies to curb the environmental impact of the clothing industry, it is important to identify the source of the problem in the supply chain.
lines.translation: 为了制定有效的政策来遏制服装行业对环境的影响，确定供应链中问题的根源至关重要。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies can then take an informed approach to recognize the environmental impact of fast-fashion and to design an ecosystem to reduce waste, incentivize innovation, and create new business models to manage waste.
lines.translation: 然后，制造商、消费者和监管机构可以采取知情的方法来认识快时尚的环境影响，并设计一个生态系统来减少浪费、激励创新以及创建新的商业模式来管理废物。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 5. Why has the clothing industry come under attack?
lines.translation: 第 5 题：为什么服装行业受到抨击?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 6. Why did the researchers put forth such policies as production tax?
lines.translation: 第 6 题：为什么研究人员提出诸如生产税之类的政策?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 7. What should be done first to eliminate the harm caused by the clothing industry?
lines.translation: 第 7 题：要消除服装行业造成的危害,首先应该做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Section B. Directions.
lines.translation: B节. 指示。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
lines.translation: 在本节中,你们将听到两次长长的谈话。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At the end of each conversation,
lines.translation: 每次谈话结束时

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: you will hear four questions.
lines.translation: 你会听到四个问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
lines.translation: 谈话和问题只谈一次

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: you hear a question,
lines.translation: 你听到一个问题,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B,
lines.translation: 你必须从四个选择中选择最好的答案 标注A,B,

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: C and D.
lines.translation: C和D。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 在答题单单行的答题表一中标出相应的字母。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conversation one.
lines.translation: 交谈之一。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Hey Mary, you seem to be very much annoyed.
lines.translation: 嘿，Mary，你看起来很烦恼。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What happened?
lines.translation: 怎么了?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Rush hour in this city is killing me.
lines.translation: 这个城市的高峰期快把我逼疯了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Ah, yes.
lines.translation: 啊，是的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Rush hour is terrible, especially in the morning between 8 and 9.
lines.translation: 高峰期确实很糟糕，尤其是早上8点到9点之间。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But what else can you expect in a city this big?
lines.translation: 但在这么大的城市里你还能指望什么呢?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, I think the local government could help improve things.
lines.translation: 嗯，我觉得当地政府可以帮忙改善一下。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I mean, getting rid of rush hour may be impossible, but it could be made more tolerable, don't you think?
lines.translation: 我的意思是，消除高峰期可能不太可能，但可以让它变得更能忍受一些，你不觉得吗?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Um… but I'm not sure how.
lines.translation: 嗯……但我不太确定怎么做。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, for example, the subway system could have air conditioning.
lines.translation: 比如说 地铁系统可以有空调

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway, so why can't we?
lines.translation: 我知道世界上很多城市的地铁里都有空调 所以为什么我们不能呢?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It gets so hot in the summer.
lines.translation: 夏天会变得这么热

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I can hardly breathe down there.
lines.translation: 我几乎喘不过气了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And add to that the rush-hour crowds with strangers packed close together in the subway carriages, the whole thing is just horrible.
lines.translation: 再加上在地铁车厢里 挤满陌生人的 匆忙的人群 整个事情都太可怕了

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Ah, yes, you are completely right.
lines.translation: 啊，是的，你说得完全对。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The trains here are too old.
lines.translation: 这里的列车太旧了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The government should definitely invest in new ones with air conditioning.
lines.translation: 政府绝对应该投资购买带空调的新列车。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I guess I'm fortunate I take the bus instead.
lines.translation: 我想我很幸运，我坐公交车。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Oh, that's much better.
lines.translation: 哦，那好多了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yeah, it's more convenient.
lines.translation: 是啊,这更方便。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Bus No.
lines.translation: 巴士号

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 36 goes straight from my house to the office.
lines.translation: 从我家直接到办公室的36个

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's a 30-minute ride and I don't have to make any changes.
lines.translation: 这是30分钟的车程 我不需要做任何改变

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That sounds nice.
lines.translation: 听起来不错。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I tell you, my current commute is killing me.
lines.translation: 告诉你，我现在的通勤快把我逼疯了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Maybe I should move closer to the office.
lines.translation: 也许我应该搬到离办公室近一点的地方。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, I know a great housing agent.
lines.translation: 嗯，我认识一个很棒的房产中介。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I found the flat I'm living in now through him.
lines.translation: 我现在住的公寓就是通过他找到的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: And I love it.
lines.translation: 我很喜欢。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Hmm, could you send me his number, please?
lines.translation: 嗯，你能把他的号码发给我吗?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Sure thing.
lines.translation: 当然可以。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Just tell him exactly what you are looking for and I'm sure he will find something good.
lines.translation: 只要告诉他你具体在找什么，我相信他会找到好房子的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 8. Why is the woman complaining?
lines.translation: 第 8 题：女士为什么在抱怨?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 9. What does the woman suggest doing?
lines.translation: 第 9 题：女士建议做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 10. What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
lines.translation: 第 10 题：从对话中我们了解到男士的什么情况?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 11. What does the woman ask the man to do at the end of the conversation?
lines.translation: 第 11 题：对话结束时女士要求男士做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Conversation two.
lines.translation: 对话二

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Did you hear about Johnny?
lines.translation: 你听说Johnny的事了吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No.
lines.translation: 没有。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why?
lines.translation: 为什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Is he okay?
lines.translation: 他还好吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He had some plastic surgery done.
lines.translation: 他做了整形手术。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What?
lines.translation: 什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Why?
lines.translation: 为什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Do you remember he had a scar on his face?
lines.translation: 你还记得他脸上有道疤吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Yes, of course.
lines.translation: 记得，当然记得。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He always had that.
lines.translation: 他一直都有那道疤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I've known him since primary school, and I always remember him having that on his cheek.
lines.translation: 我从小学就认识他了，一直记得他脸颊上有那道疤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Well, he had it fixed.
lines.translation: 嗯，他把它修复了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Fixed?
lines.translation: 修复？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What do you mean?
lines.translation: 什么意思？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You can't fix a scar.
lines.translation: 疤痕是修复不了的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You know what I mean?
lines.translation: 你懂我的意思吧？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery, in order to cover it and make it less noticeable.
lines.translation: 他做了个手术，整形手术，用来遮盖疤痕，让它不那么明显。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Oh, well, that's ridiculous, isn't it?
lines.translation: 哦，这太荒唐了，不是吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It was noticeable, sure.
lines.translation: 那道疤确实挺明显的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But it wasn't an ugly scar.
lines.translation: 但它并不丑。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It never occurred to me that he should have it taken care of like that.
lines.translation: 我从来没想过他应该那样处理它。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I agree.
lines.translation: 我同意。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: I can understand some scars and physical defects can be ugly and distracting, but not Johnny's.
lines.translation: 我能理解有些疤痕和身体缺陷可能很丑、很扎眼，但Johnny的不是。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness.
lines.translation: 事实上，我觉得那道疤为他增添了个性……让他有了某种独特性。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He must have felt differently though.
lines.translation: 但他肯定想法不一样。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He must have felt self-conscious and insecure, perhaps.
lines.translation: 他可能觉得难为情、不自信吧。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: No, no, that's not the reason.
lines.translation: 不，不，不是那个原因。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: He was totally fine with his scar.
lines.translation: 他对自己的疤完全没问题。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: As you said, he had had it for most of his life.
lines.translation: 就像你说的，他大半辈子都带着那道疤。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Then why did he have the operation?
lines.translation: 那他为什么要做手术？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Because his girlfriend wanted him to.
lines.translation: 因为他女朋友想让他做。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What?
lines.translation: 什么？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's so superficial and selfish of her.
lines.translation: 她也太肤浅、太自私了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: If Johnny's girlfriend doesn't like him for who he is, then she does not deserve to be his girlfriend.
lines.translation: 如果Johnny的女朋友不喜欢真实的他，那她就不配做他女朋友。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: You are right.
lines.translation: 你说得对。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: So he is insane to give in to her like that.
lines.translation: 所以他那样向她妥协简直疯了。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But when I told him, he said he loves her and would just do what she wants him to.
lines.translation: 但当我跟他说的时候，他说他爱她，愿意做她想让他做的事。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: What a fool he is.
lines.translation: 他真是个傻瓜。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
lines.translation: 问题12到15 是基于你刚才听到的谈话

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 12. What does the man say about Johnny?
lines.translation: 第 12 题：男士对Johnny说了什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 13. What does the woman find puzzling?
lines.translation: 第 13 题：女士觉得什么令人困惑?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 14. What did the man think of Johnny's scar?
lines.translation: 第 14 题：男士对Johnny的疤痕有何看法?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 15. How could we describe the speakers' attitude towards Johnny's girlfriend?
lines.translation: 第 15 题：我们可以如何描述说话者对Johnny女友的态度?

lines.text: After you hear a question,
lines.translation: 在你听到一个问题之后

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
lines.translation: 您必须选择四个选择中的最佳答案,即A、B、C和D。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
lines.translation: 在答题单单行的答题表一中标出相应的字母。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Talking is unique to humans.
lines.translation: 说话是人类独有的

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: An animal might make 10 different sounds, but an adult human knows more than 20,000 words.
lines.translation: 动物可能发出10种不同的声音 但成年人知道超过20,000个字

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Additionally, we're the only animal that expresses thoughts in full sentences.
lines.translation: 此外,我们是唯一一个在句子上表达想法的动物。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers don't think language was invented; instead, they think it evolved.
lines.translation: 研究人员不认为语言是被发明的, 相反,他们认为语言是进化的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: How did talking evolve?
lines.translation: 谈话是如何演变的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: There are two main theories.
lines.translation: 有两个主要理论。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The first theory is that language started with people making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them, like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools.
lines.translation: 第一种理论认为,语言起源于人们发出不同的声音,主要是模仿周围的事物,比如动物叫声、自然界的声音以及工具的声音。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Perhaps they made the sound of wind to comment on the weather or imitated the sound of a bird to tell a friend that there was a bird nearby.
lines.translation: 也许他们发出风的声音来评论天气,或者模仿鸟叫声来告诉朋友附近有一只鸟。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Then over hundreds of thousands of years, those sounds turned into words that people began to learn as part of their language.
lines.translation: 然后在数十万年的时间里,这些声音演变成了词汇,人们开始将其作为语言的一部分来学习。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At some point, people started stringing the words together to form sentences.
lines.translation: 在某个时刻,人们开始将词汇串联起来形成句子。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The other main theory, which is more recent, is that people started off by gesturing—pointing at things with their hands and imitating actions using their bodies.
lines.translation: 另一种主要理论更为近期,认为人们最初是通过手势——用手指向事物并用身体模仿动作来交流的。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Eventually these gestures turned into a full sign language.
lines.translation: 最终这些手势演变成了完整的手语。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This theory guesses that after developing sign languages, people eventually started making sounds along with their gestures.
lines.translation: 这个理论推测,在发展出手语之后,人们最终开始在做手势的同时发出声音。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At some point, they switched to mostly making sounds that became words instead of just using their bodies.
lines.translation: 在某个时刻,他们转变为主要发出声音形成词汇,而不仅仅是使用身体。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you communicate with someone even when you can't see them.
lines.translation: 该理论认为,他们转向发出声音的原因是,出声说话可以让你即使在看不见对方的情况下也能进行交流。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 16. How did language come into being according to researchers?
lines.translation: 第 16 题：根据研究人员的说法,语言是如何产生的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 17. How did language start according to the first theory?
lines.translation: 第 17 题：根据第一种理论,语言是如何起源的?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 18. Why did people switch from gesturing to making sounds according to the more recent theory?
lines.translation: 第 18 题：根据较新的理论,人们为什么从做手势转向发出声音?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Is it a good idea to display luxury brands and other signals of status?
lines.translation: 展示奢侈品牌和其他地位象征是个好主意吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Is it a good idea to display luxury brands and other signals of status?
lines.translation: 展示奢侈品牌和其他地位象征是个好主意吗？

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It depends on the situation.
lines.translation: 这取决于具体情况。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Studies have shown that people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent, disciplined, and competent than those who do not.
lines.translation: 研究表明,看起来富有的人往往被认为比那些看起来不富有的人更聪明、更自律、更有能力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But new research found that people believe someone who shows off their social status cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others.
lines.translation: 但新研究发现,人们认为炫耀社会地位的人更关心自身利益而非帮助他人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This means people are less willing to collaborate with them.
lines.translation: 这意味着人们不太愿意与他们合作。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Modesty may be key when cooperation is essential, but the researchers also found that in some cases, status signaling has advantages.
lines.translation: 当合作至关重要时,谦逊可能是关键,但研究人员也发现,在某些情况下,地位信号具有优势。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Experiments showed that participants were less likely to choose someone who signals their wealth or status to join a group seeking cooperative members.
lines.translation: 实验表明,当参与者寻找合作型成员加入团队时,他们不太可能选择那些展示财富或地位的人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But participants were more likely to choose that person when they're looking for a competitive team member.
lines.translation: 但当他们寻找竞争型团队成员时,参与者更有可能选择那个人。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: These findings suggest that people should change how they present themselves depending on their social goal.
lines.translation: 这些发现表明,人们应该根据自己的社交目标来改变展示自己的方式。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This is the era of social media.
lines.translation: 这是社交媒体的时代。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: People can easily share their wealth and status to large audiences, but they need to consider the consequences.
lines.translation: 人们可以轻松地向广大受众分享自己的财富和地位,但他们需要考虑后果。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Posting about luxury purchases and expensive vacations online may help you to persuade others and frighten competitors, but it could also signal to potential friends or future employers that you are unlikely to think about the needs of others.
lines.translation: 在网上发布关于奢侈品购买和昂贵假期的内容可能有助于你说服他人并威慑竞争对手,但它也可能向潜在朋友或未来雇主发出信号,表明你不太可能考虑他人的需求。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This makes things tricky for people who may want to impress others while also demonstrating that they are a team player.
lines.translation: 这使得那些既想给他人留下深刻印象又想表明自己是团队合作者的人处境尴尬。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.
lines.translation: 19至21是根据你刚才听到的段落

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 19. How would people describe someone who shows off their social status according to new research?
lines.translation: 第 19 题：根据新研究,人们会如何描述炫耀自己社会地位的人?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 20. When were participants more likely to choose someone who signaled their wealth or status?
lines.translation: 第 20 题：参与者在什么情况下更可能选择那些展示自己财富或地位的人?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 21. What should people do when sharing their wealth and status online?
lines.translation: 第 21 题：人们在网上分享自己的财富和地位时应该做什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Human fascination with animals goes back as far as humans do.
lines.translation: 人类对动物的迷恋可以追溯到人类诞生之初。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Of the oldest cave paintings discovered, some are up to 40,000 years old, and there are more images of animals than humans.
lines.translation: 在已发现的最古老洞穴壁画中,有些距今已有4万年之久,其中动物图像多于人类图像。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: At some point, humans began to capture and hold animals.
lines.translation: 在某个时期,人类开始捕获和饲养动物。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The first-known collections were held by royalty and were not open to the public.
lines.translation: 已知最早的动物收藏由王室持有,不对公众开放。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In Egypt, researchers have found buildings from around 3500 B.C., containing the remains of animals, including elephants, which were not native to Egypt.
lines.translation: 在埃及,研究人员发现了约公元前3500年的建筑,其中存有动物遗骸,包括并非埃及本土物种的大象。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: But life wasn't easy for these animals.
lines.translation: 但这些动物的生活并不轻松。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: They probably had short lives, and their remains show evidence of severe injuries.
lines.translation: 它们的寿命可能很短,其遗骸显示出严重受伤的痕迹。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The first public exhibit of animals may have been created by Egypt's Queen Hatshepsut around 1480 B.C.
lines.translation: 首个向公众展出的动物园可能由埃及女王Hatshepsut于公元前1480年左右建造。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Researchers think the zoo was started with animals brought home from a far-off land known as Punt.
lines.translation: 研究人员认为该动物园始于从一个名为Punt的遥远之地带回的动物。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It's unclear why the Queen built the zoo, but it might have been to show off her wealth and power.
lines.translation: 女王建造动物园的原因尚不清楚,但可能是为了炫耀她的财富和权力。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: Early zoos are found all over the world.
lines.translation: 早期动物园遍布世界各地

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In China, Emperor Wenwang is said to have built a "Garden of Intelligence" around 1060 B.C.
lines.translation: 在中国,文旺皇帝据说在公元前10点60分左右 建造了一个"情报之宝"

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: It included deer, birds, and many fish.
lines.translation: 它包括鹿、鸟和许多鱼。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals in about 1110 as part of the royal estate.
lines.translation: 在英国,亨利国王... ...我在1110年左右 建立了一批动物... ...作为皇家遗产的一部分

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: His collection included tigers and lions.
lines.translation: 他的收藏品包括老虎和狮子。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: This collection eventually moved to the Tower of London in 1235.
lines.translation: 这个收藏最终于1235年搬到伦敦塔

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: The collection stayed at that location for 600 years.
lines.translation: 该收藏在该地点存放了600年。

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 22. What can we see in the oldest cave paintings?
lines.translation: 第 22 题：我们能在最古老的洞穴壁画中看到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 23. What do we learn about the first-known collections of animals?
lines.translation: 第 23 题：关于最早已知的动物收藏,我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 24. What might be the reason the Egyptian Queen created the zoo?
lines.translation: 第 24 题：埃及女王创建动物园的原因可能是什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: 25. What do we learn about King Henry I's collection of animals in England?
lines.translation: 第 25 题：关于英格兰国王亨利一世的动物收藏,我们了解到什么?

lines.speaker: 听力原声
lines.text: That's the end of listening comprehension.
lines.translation: 听觉理解到此结束
